Love your videos. My quick research appears to exclude the Mojave:  U.S. Geological Survey (USGS): The USGS explicitly lists California's deserts as three distinct, separate entities: the Great Basin Desert, the Mojave Desert, and the Colorado Desert (a subdivision of the Sonoran Desert).  
 National Park Service (NPS) Geodiversity Atlas: The NPS defines the Mojave Desert as a distinct region that is bounded on the north by the Great Basin, noting that while they share geological ties via the broader Basin and Range tectonic province, they are separate ecological provinces.

comments.author: @captainfantastic7843
comments.text:
Actually, Lake Lahonton was largely dried up by 9000-10,000 years ago. Not quite, but almost.

The peak of Lake Lahonton's existence was much earlier than that, about 20,000 years ago.

This is why my archeological partner and I were able to discover primitive, stone tools scattered along the old beach terraces of Lake Lahonton that are located at high altitudes, along mountain tops in the Great Basin.  This became some of the first irrefutable proof that there were different peoples here before those who claim the "Native American" label. 

According to linguistic professors we worked with at University Nevada Reno, the closest living relatives to the people who inhabited this portion of the globe before the so-called native Americans are the Washo Indians who's language is an entirely distinct branch than that of all the other tribes in the region. 

The Bureau of Land Management head of archaeology just about shit his pants when we disclosed the obvious evidence to him roughly 26 years ago. 

This put to rest the predominant theory at the time that there were no humans on this continent before 11.5 thousand years ago. A theory that we took issue with and challenged and offered some solid evidence towards. Oh the arguments we'd get in with professors who thought they knew it all. 

It was a lot of fun and incredibly interesting. And incredibly gratifying to resolve the idea that the natives were not "first peoples" after all, 

It all makes one thank God for white colonists! 😉👍🏼🇺🇸
